name: Zoledronic acid
route_note: IV infusion over at least 15 minutes: 5 mg once yearly for osteoporosis; 4 mg every 3–4 weeks in cancer

discovery.note: The most potent bisphosphonate in clinical use, with an imidazole ring side chain.

tagline: A once-a-year bisphosphonate infusion for osteoporosis and bone metastases
summary: Zoledronic acid is the most potent nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate and is given as an intravenous infusion. In oncology it treats hypercalcaemia of malignancy and prevents skeletal events from bone metastases and myeloma; a single yearly infusion reduces fractures in osteoporosis.
mechanism: Bisphosphonates are analogues of pyrophosphate that bind avidly to hydroxyapatite at sites of active bone remodelling. When osteoclasts resorb bone they take up the drug, and nitrogen-containing bisphosphonates inhibit farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase (FDPS) in the mevalonate pathway, blocking prenylation of small GTPases needed for osteoclast function and survival.
Its high binding affinity and potency allow infrequent dosing, and in cancer it reduces tumour-driven osteolysis and the release of calcium from bone.
uses: Bone metastases from solid tumours and multiple myeloma (prevention of skeletal-related events)

history.title: Zometa approved
history.detail: FDA approves Zometa for hypercalcaemia of malignancy in August 2001, extended to bone metastases in 2002.

history.title: Paget's disease
history.detail: Aclasta is approved in the EU for Paget's disease of bone.

history.title: HORIZON trials
history.detail: HORIZON-PFT shows yearly zoledronic acid cuts vertebral fractures by 70%; FDA approves Reclast for osteoporosis.

history.title: Mortality after hip fracture
history.detail: HORIZON-RFT shows reduced new fractures and mortality after hip fracture.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic zoledronic acid enters the US market.

history.title: Osteopenia trial
history.detail: A New Zealand trial shows zoledronic acid every 18 months reduces fractures in older women with osteopenia (NEJM 2018).

pk.half_life: triphasic; terminal about 146 h in plasma, years in bone
pk.excretion: about 40% unchanged in urine within 24 h; remainder bound to bone

common: acute-phase reaction (fever, myalgia, flu-like symptoms) after first infusion

facts: A single 5 mg infusion maintains anti-fracture effect for at least a year.
Osteonecrosis of the jaw is considerably more frequent at oncology doses than osteoporosis doses.

references.title: Black DM et al. HORIZON Pivotal Fracture Trial (NEJM 2007)
